cyp_profile.pathway_evidence: Eprinomectin is a P-glycoprotein substrate and inhibitor. Praziquantel is metabolized via CYP3A and is a substrate of CYP 3A4 in humans.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Eprinomectin undergoes minimal biotransformation and is excreted primarily in feces as unchanged drug. Praziquantel is excreted primarily in the urine.

organ_burden_logic.note: Based on pharmacokinetics and reported adverse effects.

brain.evidence: Not labeled for dogs; no specific dog burden data provided other than praziquantel half-life and vomiting at high doses.
Transient ataxia, disorientation, lethargy, and pupil dilation have been noted at higher doses.

kidney.evidence: Praziquantel is excreted primarily in urine, but no nephrotoxicity is reported.

liver.evidence: Praziquantel is metabolized in the liver via CYP3A enzymes.

timing_profile.evidence: In cats, topical eprinomectin Cmax was reached on average after 24 hours. Terminal half-life was 114 hours (topical). Bioavailability 31%. Protein binding >99%. Praziquantel elimination half-life is ~3 hours in dogs.

drug_interactions.evidence: Praziquantel may increase albendazole sulphoxide concentration.
May increase the serum concentration of praziquantel.
May decrease eprinomectin and/or praziquantel concentrations.

drug_interactions.drug: CYP3A4 Inhibitors (amiodarone, clarithromycin, fluoxetine, itraconazole, ketoconazole, verapamil)
drug_interactions.evidence: May increase eprinomectin and/or praziquantel concentrations.
Can significantly increase praziquantel serum concentrations. May increase eprinomectin concentrations.

drug_interactions.drug: P-Glycoprotein Inhibitors (amiodarone, cyclosporine, digoxin, itraconazole, spironolactone)
P-Glycoprotein Substrates (cyclosporine, doxorubicin, mitoxantrone, phenothiazines, vinca alkaloids)
drug_interactions.evidence: Eprinomectin may inhibit P-glycoprotein and increase exposure to P-glycoprotein substrates.

dosage_list.context: Prevention of heartworm disease, and treatment/control of roundworms, hookworms, and tapeworms
dosage_list.frequency: Monthly for prevention/control; Once for treatment
dosage_list.duration_note: Apply directly on the skin in 1 spot on the midline of the neck.
dosage_list.evidence: Delivers a minimum dose of eprinomectin 0.5 mg/kg and praziquantel 10 mg/kg.

hepatic_dose_adjustment.note: Praziquantel is metabolized in the liver via CYP3A; no specific adjustment guidelines provided, but liver function may affect clearance.

genetic_sensitivity.evidence: Eprinomectin is a P-glycoprotein substrate and inhibitor, which implies potential sensitivity in animals with MDR1 mutations (though typically more of a concern in dogs).

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Eprinomectin binds to glutamate-gated chloride ion channels in invertebrate nerve/muscle cells, increasing chloride permeability and causing paralysis. Praziquantel interacts with integument phospholipids, causing calcium ion flux and disintegration of the cestode.

species_notes.dog: Not indicated or labeled for use in dogs.
species_notes.cat: For use in cats and kittens 7 weeks and older and 0.8 kg or greater. Do not administer orally.

cat.evidence: Do not use in kittens <7 weeks or weighing <0.8 kg. Do not administer orally. Prevent licking of the application site.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store protected from light at or below 30°C (86°F) with excursions permitted to 40°C (104°F).

section_1_2_10.highlights: Topical feline heartworm preventive, also treats and controls roundworms, hookworms, and tapeworms. For use in cats and kittens 7 weeks and older and 0.8 kg (1.8 lb) or greater. Usually well tolerated; salivation may occur if cats lick the application site.
section_1_2_10.indications: Prevention of heartworm disease caused by Dirofilaria immitis, and treatment and control of roundworms, hookworms, and tapeworms in cats and kittens 7 weeks of age and older and >= 0.8 kg.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Administer year-round or start 1 month before mosquito exposure. Apply directly to skin between base of skull and shoulder blades. Prevent licking. Ingested product can cause salivation, vomiting, and lack of energy. Wash hands after applying.
